QUOTE: When it is defined, the wrapper expands to the plain member name. ... In the default configuration it expands to `private_##member`... Application code in the wild never gets it unless it defines the macro itself before including mbedtls headers.

VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that defining MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS gives plain member names, while the default configuration gives private_-renamed names. It also says ordinary application code doesn't get the opt-out unless it defines the macro itself.
